# Fairpractice Secondary Claims (`fairpractice-secondary-claims`)

Checks secondary and tertiary claims: balances left after the primary pays with no claim to the next payer (and the filing window for it), claims to the next payer sent before the primary adjudicated or without its EOB, and payers billed in the wrong order against the coverage on file. Patient names are masked before results reach the model.

**Fairpractice Secondary Claims never submits or changes claims. Fairpractice Secondary Claims never bills patients.**

Fairpractice ver 1 · Money recovery and practice finance · MIT · Node 20 or newer · local files only · patient and staff identifiers masked before results reach the model · built on [`fairpractice-core`](../fairpractice-core)

```bash
npx -y fairpractice-secondary-claims demo
npx -y fairpractice-secondary-claims mcp --root ./practice-files
```

## What the sample data shows

Fictional data only: a made-up practice, patients and payers. Any likeness to real people is chance. Filing windows in the settings are examples, not any payer's rule.

- [`claims.csv`](fixtures/claims.csv) and [`coverage.csv`](fixtures/coverage.csv). Planted (as of November 15, 2026):
  - S1: 120 left after the primary paid October 1; the Cedar Supplement claim (60 days) is due November 30.
  - S2: 200 left after the primary paid August 1; the Cedar Supplement claim was due September 30 and was never sent.
  - S3: 80 left after the primary paid November 1; no State Medicaid claim yet (365 days).
  - S4: billed to Cedar Supplement as primary, but coverage has it as secondary.
  - S5: the Cedar Supplement claim was sent October 5, a week before the primary adjudicated.
  - S6: billed in the right order with the EOB, and is fine.
- [`settings.json`](fixtures/settings.json): 90 days by default, 60 for Cedar Supplement, 365 for State Medicaid, 21-day warning. [`settings-typo.json`](fixtures/settings-typo.json) misspells a setting and is refused.

## Tools

| Tool | What it does | Policy |
|---|---|---|
| `secondary_check` | List missed and closing secondary filing windows, wrong payer order, secondaries not sent and secondaries sent too early. | runs |
| `secondary_write_report` | Write secondary-claims.csv (one row per item, with blank owner and decision columns) and secondary-claims.html into out_dir (default kestrel-out/secondary). | runs |
| `secondary_recall` | Search this agent's own memory of the customer's setup: accepted facts (in use) and facts waiting for a person. | runs |
| `secondary_learn` | Propose one fact about the customer's setup for this agent to remember. | runs |
| `secondary_accept_learning` | A named person accepts or rejects a fact waiting in this agent's memory. | one named click, even in Auto (`accept_learning`) |
| `secondary_retire_memory` | A named person stops an accepted fact from applying. | one named click, even in Auto (`accept_learning`) |
| `claim_submit` | Fairpractice Secondary Claims never submits or changes claims. | refused |
| `patient_statement_send` | Fairpractice Secondary Claims never bills patients. | refused |

Any tool name not in this table is blocked, including names a model invents. Refused tools are listed so a model can see they exist and are refused.

### `secondary_check` arguments

| Argument | What it is |
|---|---|
| `claims` (required) | Claim headers under --root: claim, patient, date of service, payer, payer order, billed, paid, patient responsibility, sent date, adjudicated date, EOB attached |
| `coverage` (required) | Coverage on file: patient, payer, order (primary, secondary, tertiary), effective and term dates |
| `settings` | Optional settings JSON: filing_days, warn_days |
| `as_of` | Date to measure deadlines and ages from (YYYY-MM-DD); default today |
| `status` | Only items with this status |
| `limit` | Most items to return to the model (the report file always has all of them) |

## Columns it reads

Tables can be CSV, TSV, semicolon- or pipe-separated text, Excel `.xlsx`, JSON or JSONL. Columns are matched by the names below (any case and punctuation), and by their usual names in German, French, Spanish, Portuguese, Italian, Japanese, Chinese and Korean. Dates become `YYYY-MM-DD`. Columns marked *masked* hold patient or staff identifiers.

The PointClickCare, MatrixCare and American HealthTech style names were written from public help pages and general knowledge, **not checked against real exports**. Run `npx fairpractice-secondary-claims inspect <file>` (column names and shapes only, never values) and name any column it misses in `remedy-sources.json`.

### Claims (`claims`)

| Column | Type | Read from |
|---|---|---|
| `claim_id` | text | Claim, Claim ID, Claim #, Claim Number, Encounter, Encounter ID, Visit ID, Invoice |
| `patient_id` | text (masked) | Patient ID, Patient #, Patient Number, MRN, Medical Record Number, Chart #, Chart Number, Account # |
| `patient_name` | text (masked) | Patient, Patient Name, Name, Client, Client Name, Member, Member Name, Beneficiary |
| `dos` (required) | date | Date of Service, DOS, Service Date, Visit Date, Date, From DOS, Session Date, Appointment Date |
| `payer` (required) | text | Payer, Payer Name, Primary Payer, Insurance, Insurance Name, Plan, Plan Name, Payor |
| `order` | text | Payer Order, Order, Sequence, COB Order, Priority, Payer Sequence |
| `billed` | amount | Charge, Charges, Billed, Billed Amount, Amount, Fee, Total Charge |
| `paid` | amount | Paid, Paid Amount, Payment, Insurance Paid, Amount Paid, Allowed Paid |
| `patient_resp` | amount | Patient Responsibility, Patient Resp, PR, Balance, Remaining Balance |
| `sent_date` | date | Sent, Sent Date, Submitted, Submission Date, Billed Date |
| `adjudicated_date` | date | Adjudicated, Adjudicated Date, Paid Date, Remit Date, EOB Date, Processed Date |
| `eob_attached` | text | EOB Attached, Primary EOB, COB Info, EOB Sent |

### Coverage (`coverage`)

| Column | Type | Read from |
|---|---|---|
| `patient_id` (required) | text (masked) | Patient ID, Patient #, Patient Number, MRN, Medical Record Number, Chart #, Chart Number, Account # |
| `patient_name` | text (masked) | Patient, Patient Name, Name, Client, Client Name, Member, Member Name, Beneficiary |
| `payer` (required) | text | Payer, Payer Name, Primary Payer, Insurance, Insurance Name, Plan, Plan Name, Payor |
| `order` (required) | text | Payer Order, Order, Sequence, COB Order, Priority, Payer Sequence |
| `effective` | date | Effective, Effective Date, Start, Start Date |
| `term` | date | Term, Term Date, End, End Date |

## Settings file (`secondary_settings`)

A small JSON file you pass by path. A misspelled setting is refused by name rather than ignored, so a typo never silently changes a check.

| Setting | What it does |
|---|---|
| `filing_days` | Days after the prior payer's adjudication to file with the next payer, by payer name, plus "default" (default 90). Set from your payer contracts. |
| `warn_days` | Days ahead to warn about a filing window closing; default 21 |

## Memory

`secondary_learn` only proposes a fact; nothing changes until a named person accepts it with `secondary_accept_learning`, which is one click even in Auto. Facts live in a hash-chained file under `.remedy/memory/`; if the chain does not verify, no fact is used. Credentials, personal identifiers and text that reads like instructions to an AI are refused.

| Kind | What an accepted fact does |
|---|---|

## Install

Node 20 or newer. No other runtime dependencies besides `fairpractice-core` and `fairclaim-core`.

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "fairpractice-secondary-claims": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": [
        "-y",
        "fairpractice-secondary-claims",
        "mcp",
        "--root",
        "/path/to/practice-files"
      ]
    }
  }
}
```

Claude Code: `claude mcp add fairpractice-secondary-claims -- npx -y fairpractice-secondary-claims mcp --root .`, or use the plugin files in this folder.

## CLI

```bash
fairpractice-secondary-claims tools                 # every tool, its policy and arguments
fairpractice-secondary-claims sources               # the columns each input is read from
fairpractice-secondary-claims inspect <file>        # how a file would be read (names and shapes, never values)
fairpractice-secondary-claims call secondary_check '{"claims":"<claims>","coverage":"<coverage>"}'
fairpractice-secondary-claims eval                  # the private eval cases on the fictional fixtures
fairpractice-secondary-claims demo
```

## Patient and staff data

Results go to an AI model, so identifiers are masked before they leave the agent: patient and staff names become stable pseudonyms such as `PT-3f9a1c2e`, record and account numbers become `MRN-…` or `ACCT-…`, and e-mails and phone numbers are removed, also inside free text. Report files written to disk keep real names because staff work from them: keep them in a folder only your staff can open. The shared tests check that no fictional identifier from the fixtures reaches any eval result, and the hostile-input check plants spreadsheet formulas, HTML and AI-aimed instructions in the data. This keeps PHI away from the model; it is **not** a HIPAA compliance determination. Your business associate agreements, access controls and policies still apply.

## Limits

- Reads only the files you give it. It does not log in to an EHR, practice-management system, payer portal, clearinghouse, state system, HR or payroll system, or bank.
- Payer, Medicare, Medicaid, state and federal rules are summarised from public material as of 2026, and the numbers are settings you supply; a billing, compliance or legal professional checks them before you rely on them.
- Not legal, billing, coding, tax, clinical or HIPAA advice. It does not diagnose or recommend care. A person decides what to bill, pay, report, file or send.
- Every call is written to a hash-chained audit log under `.remedy/` in the root. No network calls, no telemetry, no credentials. The bundled data is fictional.
